correctness.rationale: For each n>=3 the white-edge bipartite graph characterization is proved from the ordinary forcing rule: no white cycles can break and a first force requires an isolate; equality in the edge bound yields exactly an isolated row/column and a spanning tree. Tree leaves provide the induction giving sufficiency. A slide shares a row/column of its removed and inserted white edges; a putative side switch necessarily shares a column and cannot create an isolated column. Repeated tree exchanges that add edges from a chosen active row to each column and then move other row leaves to a chosen column build a canonical double star without leaving the tree class. One move changes missing row using a third row for n>=3, and one non-slide jump trades a leaf column for the formerly missing row. n=2 treated separately. Two independently implemented exhaustive methods agree for n=2,3,4, but finite tests are not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The exact structural obstruction to moving optimal zero-forcing placements by adjacent-token slides, in contrast with global single-token jumps, is a natural reconfiguration question not answered by known optimal cardinality or count. The nontrivial all-parameter double-star pivot argument supplies constructive connectivity within each orientation, and the sharp n=2 exception gives a meaningful family boundary. This is not a re-expression of the already published polynomial or an arbitrary tiny finite invariant.
